says: In next/, the Effect sweep's preferEffect* fixes rewrite code inside Playwright callbacks that run in the browser (page.evaluate and the like), where module imports do not exist, and no lint, type or plain test sees it; only the visual laws fail at run time. Seen twice on 2026-11-18: PR 1562 (Rec.fromEntries in tezgah.test-support.ts statusBar, Rec.values in tuval's key.laws.visual.test.ts) and PR 1593 (Predicate). The Effect diagnostics also flag native calls inside those callbacks, so they push the wrong fix.
proof: CI run https://github.com/kamp-us/tea-fabrika/actions/runs/44244898620, job next (e2e-1): tezgah-focus.visual.test.ts fails at tezgah.test-support.ts:676 with `page.evaluate: ReferenceError: __vite_ssr_import_3__ is not defined`; at 6e753735880cb2692e3cd7c12ce6c337e9a9de31 line 677 reads `const tiles = Rec.fromEntries(` inside `on.evaluate(() => {`, where main had `Object.fromEntries`; the fix at a6cb7c62773a290b57446a795506fe0f34337c80 restores it and the law passes, and a planted Rec.fromEntries fails it again.
cost: Each sweep slice that touches e2e helpers can break a visual law that only CI's visual legs run; a lint rule refusing imported bindings inside these callbacks, or an exception the Effect checks honor there, would catch it before review.
